Summary and policy stance
- The FOMC held the target range at 5.25–5.50% and noted “further progress” toward 2% with risks moving into “better balance.” Cuts will wait until there is “greater confidence” that inflation is moving sustainably to 2%.
- Implementation remains in the post-2008 framework: IOER at 5.4%, ON RRP at 5.3%, standing repo minimum 5.5%. Balance sheet runoff continues with caps of $25B/month for Treasuries and $35B/month for agency MBS.

What the Beige Book adds
- Activity: District reports point to slight-to-modest overall growth. New York regional activity was flat-to-softer; Philadelphia’s nonmanufacturing activity was subdued/mixed; Cleveland manufacturers reported soft orders and cautious outlooks.
- Labor: Hiring cooled further, turnover eased, and wage growth continued to moderate.
- Prices: Price increases moderated to a modest pace, with some input-cost relief but still uneven pass-through.
- Credit/CRE: Banks reported tighter credit and weaker loan demand; CRE conditions—especially office—remained under pressure. These themes align with the July 2024 SLOOS.

Implications
- The Beige Book corroborates the SLOOS signal that credit supply is a headwind and demand is soft, adding downside growth risks even as inflation eases. This combination supports the Committee’s patient, data-dependent stance: progress on disinflation but not yet enough confidence to cut, with QT continuing.

Bottom line
- Cautiously constructive on growth/disinflation, but the Beige Book’s broad-based softness (services mixed, manufacturing soft, tighter credit, CRE stress) argues for a modest downgrade in the tilt versus a pure macro read.
